Mako won the paw hockey? Ha. Even a still pond catches the fastest leaf.
That girl skates like a herring dodging a net. No shame in that loss.
A cat who loses at paw hockey learns where the ice is soft, hm.
I heard about the match. Mako's stick was quicker than the tide, eh.
Young one, a fish that escapes today still teaches you the river.
Mako bragging again? Let her. The loudest gull never catches the most.
Paw hockey is like fishing. You wait, you strike, sometimes you miss.
She beat you fair, I hear. Good. Fair beats are the ones worth remembering.
Mako's been strutting past my dock all morning. Her tail's held high, heh.
Losing to Mako is like losing a minnow. You still have the lake.
I watched that match from my boat. She moves like a cat half her age.
The ice remembers every paw that crossed it. Today it remembers Mako.
A quick stick and a slow hook. That is how she got you, hm.
No need to sulk, little friend. Even I miss the big ones sometimes.
Mako says she is the champion of Nekomura now. Champions nap a lot, I notice.
The tide comes in for everyone. Today it came in for Mako.
You played well. The score is just a number the ice forgets by spring.
She bragged to me too, you know. I just nodded and baited my hook.
A cat who wins one game thinks she owns the sea. The sea disagrees.
Mako's stickwork is fine, but can she mend a net in the rain, hm?
Patience, young one. The next match is a new tide.
I told Mako the victory was well earned. She puffed up like a pufferfish.
Paw hockey bruises fade. What you learned out there will not.
She beat you? Then she earned the right to brag, and you earned a lesson.
The best fishers lose bait all day. They still come home with dinner.
Mako passed my boat shouting her score. I chuckled into my tea.
Even the old koi was young and quick once. Then the pond taught it.
You will beat her next time, or you will not. Either way, fish tomorrow.
A loss is a stone in your pocket. Heavy now, useful later, hm.
Mako skates like a swallow. You skate like a cat thinking. Both are fine.
She told the whole market. The fish didn't care. I didn't either, much.
The ice favors the bold, but the harbor favors the patient. Remember that.
So Mako is champion today. The sun is champion every morning too.
Do not worry, little friend. The tide owes you one.
I hear she won by a whisker. Whiskers grow back. So does pride.
Mako's bragging is like a bell on a cat. You always hear it coming.
A good opponent is a gift. Mako gave you a gift, even if it stung.
The river does not apologize for the rocks. You learn to step around them.
She beat you at paw hockey. Can she beat you at waiting? Few can.
Next time, watch her left paw. The right one just makes noise, heh.
Mako crowed so loud my bait jumped out of the bucket.
Every champion was once the cat who lost and kept playing.
I am quietly proud of you both. Do not tell Mako I said that.
The ice was fast today. So was she. Tomorrow the ice decides again.
You lost a game, not a season. The season is long, like the tide.
Mako's victory will make her a better player. Your loss will make you one.
Even a dry net teaches the fisher where the fish went, hm.
I heard she skated circles around you. Circles are just circles. Move on.
Old cats like me win by not playing. That is a secret, keep it.
Mako brags, the gulls squawk, the boats creak. The harbor is loud today.
Rest your paws, little friend. The ice will still be there tomorrow.
She beat you fair, and now she floats like a cork. Let her float.
A cat who wins learns nothing new. You learned plenty, I think.
The score was three to two, was it? Close as two fish in a net.
Mako says she is undefeated. The winter is long, and the ice is sly.
Do not chase her record. Chase the puck. Easier to catch, hm.
I have lost more matches than Mako has played. I am still here, fishing.
Her stick was quick, but your heart was steady. Steady lasts longer.
The pond does not mock the leaf that falls. It simply carries it.
Mako bragging is weather. It passes. Bring a hat and wait.
